subject.title: [Bug]: MidTurnPrecheckSignal leaks error to UI via pushLoopFailure before internal retry completes

question: Should the durable fix for this issue be accepted as the generic agent-core control-flow-error seam in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101648, or should maintainers require an embedded-runner-owned recovery boundary instead?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the remaining choice affects the ownership boundary between reusable agent-core failure projection and embedded-runner-specific mid-turn recovery.

options.title: Require live proof for the current PR
options.body: Keep the current narrow agent-core seam as the candidate, but require redacted Gateway+MCP large-tool-output proof before merge.

options.title: Move handling into embedded runner
options.body: Ask for a replacement or revision that prevents this control signal from reaching agent-core’s generic failure handler at all.

options.title: Wait for broader compaction work
options.body: Defer this issue to broader mid-turn precheck compaction work only if that PR becomes proof-positive and mergeable.

recommendation.title: Require live proof for the current PR
recommendation.body: Keep the current narrow agent-core seam as the candidate, but require redacted Gateway+MCP large-tool-output proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is tied to the original mid-turn precheck path and related broader mid-turn precheck work, making them the best available routing owner for the boundary choice.
